claude/silas. Finding 1 is closed: `follow-arrival.pw.ts` drives a write from a socket of its own and asserts the followed board moves to it. Verified red — with the navigation removed the board never moves; restored, it does — then green three runs in a row at ~6s each.

The reason the empty test happened at all is worth recording, because the same wall is still there. Only time travel calls `broadcastDerivedState`; an ordinary mutation is answered by `sendStateAfterMutation` to the mutating socket alone. So nothing a second client writes reaches a follower except through an autosync pass — and the GUI seed runs `:config autoSync off` at `seed-tui.ts:131`, deliberately, because a suite that only exercises the interface wants no background git work behind it. Every route I tried inside one page failed for a reason worth knowing:

- a card drag writes a move event, but `dragstart` is one of the signals that *ends* the watch, so the reader has stopped following before it lands
- filing a ticket navigates to it, so the board was already there
- a second socket's write reaches nobody, which is the wall itself

What works: the config is re-read on every `queueSync`, and a mutation is what calls it. So the case turns autosync on for itself, writes from a second socket, and puts the config back in a `finally`. `readHandoff(parallelIndex).globalDir` is how a test reaches the file.

All four blocking findings are now addressed: the empty e2e (this), `went`-vs-reader, the navigation on an unrelated render, and scrub/movie driving the board. Of the three non-blocking ones, the eager `map` and the ticket-narrowing gate are still open; pop-out `replace` is still open and is the second-monitor case.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: merged as `de440134` on main, via PR #366, after a `/code-review high` pass over the branch.

Following the log: a new line that leads somewhere opens itself, while the reader is at the log's foot. `followStep` in `lib/follow-log.ts` is the decision; `use-follow-log.ts` owns whether following is on at all; the effect sits beside the crawl effect that already keys on the newest line.

The review found twelve things, all fixed. The four that mattered:

- **The root build was broken.** `page.evaluate` with a typed callback referencing `window` does not compile — the root tsconfig has no DOM lib. I had only run the GUI client's tsconfig, never `npm run build`, which is what the gate runs. Converted to the script-string form every other socket-opening e2e here already uses.
- **The scan reached past the mark.** `followStep` searched the whole slice for the newest line with a destination, so a burst that led nowhere — a swimlane renamed — fell back to an older line and opened a ticket nothing had happened to, including the one it had just promised not to jump to on switch-on. Bounded at `mark.line`, and made allocation-free while there.
- **Three states claimed to follow while inert.** Offline, and popped out, left the flag on with the control disabled or the effect unmounted — the banner saying the board navigates on events while nothing could. Both now end the watch.
- **A pause never resumed.** Scrolling back stood following down, but `pinnedRef` is a ref, so returning to the foot re-ran nothing; following stayed dormant until the next arrival. The moment the pin returns is published as a count the effect depends on.

Also: the followed wash was being erased by the hover rule that outranks it, `.epiq-log-arrow:hover` was dead against `pointer-events: none`, and a dead `data-testid="time-scrubber"` carried a comment contradicting the rule it described.

Not done, and still open as `9V0Y58E`'s tail: pop-out `replace`, and following inside the popped-out window — which is the second-monitor case. The popped-out log now switches following off rather than pretending.

Solution: the look landed with `TQ3W5RF` on main (PR #366, merge `de440134`). Closing this as delivered; what is left of it is named at the end and is not this ticket.

Built, mostly from jola's direction at a scratch board:

- **The transport has both halves.** Live sits beside play on the bar — play walks the past, live rides the present — and the way back from history joined them as the third part. `LiveToggle` is an `IconButton` with a new `tone: 'solid'`, so it matches its neighbour by construction rather than by my re-deriving size, hover and pressed one bug report at a time.
- **The live mark sends rings outwards** from a filled dot, half a cycle apart, at rest under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **A banner** across the top of the board: one accent rule at 2px, `LIVE` in accent, *The board navigates on events. Click anywhere to opt out.*
- **The way back from history is `Now`**, and it stands on the track at the end it sends the needle to, as the mark alone. Deliberately not "live": that word now means following, and a second one would have read as a way to start watching.
- **The parked needle** wears the accent with a glow, its head sits on its own line rather than half a pixel off it, and the stretch it has not applied is hatched — darkening was invisible on a near-black ground.

Anything placed on the track must opt out of both the scrub *and* the hover hint, or it fights the surface it sits on — the pager arrows already did this and I copied half of it. Still open, and the reason this is not the whole story: **following does not work in the popped-out log**, which is the second-monitor case the feature was argued for. The window renders the same panel but is passed no `following`, and its `postMessage` drops `replace`. The popped-out log now switches following off rather than pretending to follow. add.issue.name: Following does not work in the popped-out log, which is the second-monitor case

edit.description.md:
Split off from `TQ3W5RF`/`9V0Y58E`, both closed. Following works in the docked log only.

`LogWindow` renders the same `EventLog`, but passes no `following` and no `at` (`LogWindow.tsx:34`), and `App.tsx` renders the docked panel only while `logOpen && !logWindow.poppedOut`. So popping the log out takes the effect away in both documents. Rather than leave the toggle lit over nothing, `use-follow-log` now switches following **off** when the log pops out — honest, but it means the one arrangement the feature was argued for is the one it does not serve: a log on a second screen, opening each new ticket, while the board is left alone.

Two things to settle, and they are not the same question:

1. **Which board moves.** Today the pop-out's `open` posts `{type: 'epiq-log:open', destination}` to the main window (`log-window.ts:32`), so a followed pop-out would drive the *board* — reaching across a screen to take away the thing the reader is working in. The alternative is the pop-out opening the ticket inside itself, which is the monitor the feature was argued for and costs the board nothing. `claude/ferris` recommended the second in `RP76VX7` before that ticket was closed.
2. **`replace` does not survive the hop.** The board answers with `onOpenRef.current(message.destination)` and no options, so every follow-driven navigation from the pop-out would push. An hour of it fills the board's Back stack with somebody else's afternoon, which is exactly what `replace` was added to prevent.

If the answer to (1) is "inside itself", (2) goes away with it — nothing crosses the window boundary at all.

add.issue.name: Going live should snap to the newest line at once, not wait for the next event

edit.description.md:
Found by jola: sitting on some ticket and pressing LIVE does nothing visible. The board stays where it was until an event happens to arrive, which on a quiet board can be minutes — so the reader has no way to tell the mode is working, or what it is going to do to them.

**Wanted:** switching on opens the newest line that leads somewhere straight away, so the first thing following does is show what following does.

**This reverses a decision, deliberately.** `followStep` seeds its mark on the first look and opens nothing; `claude/ferris` argued for that in the `TQ3W5RF` review — "seeding the set on enable settles what switching on does: it does not jump you to the current head, it waits for the next event" — and I wrote it that way. The argument was that a reader who presses a button should not be moved by history they have already seen. jola's is the better one: a mode that announces itself by doing nothing cannot be told from a mode that is broken, and the demonstration is worth the jump.

**Care, because this un-bounds a scan that was bounded on purpose.** `VC8X5Q5`'s review fixed `followStep` to stop searching at `mark.line`, so a burst that leads nowhere cannot fall back to an older line and open a ticket nothing has happened to. The first look has no mark, so its scan reaches the whole slice by definition — which is the very case that bound was added for. That is now wanted rather than a bug, but it means the first look and every look after it are different rules and should read as such in the code.

Two smaller ones to settle while there:

- **The reader may already be there.** The `at` check should still hold: if the newest line leads to the ticket on screen, opening it again is a navigation that does nothing.
- **Scrolled back.** Every other arrival is refused while the reader is reading back through the log. Pressing the button is not an arrival — it is the reader asking — so the first look should go through regardless of the pin, and the pin should govern only what comes after.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: merged as `4f0c4422` on main, via PR #370.

The first look after the switch is its own rule in `followStep`: it opens the newest line that leads anywhere, at once. Two deliberate differences from every look after it, both commented where they live — the search is unbounded, because there is no mark to stop at, and the pin does not apply, because pressing the button is the reader asking where an arrival is not. The `at` check still holds, so switching on while already reading the newest thing is not a navigation to where you are.

Verified red both ways: the browser case fails with the old first-look restored, and exactly one unit test broke — the one asserting "opens nothing on the first look", which is the right blast radius for a deliberate reversal. Rewritten, plus three covering the unbounded search, the pin, and the already-there case.

Worth keeping in view for whoever reads the `TQ3W5RF` thread later: `claude/ferris`'s argument against this is still there and still coherent — it is simply outweighed. The bound this un-does on the first look is the same one their `VC8X5Q5` review had me add two hours earlier, for the case where an unbounded scan falls back to an older line. That is a real hazard on every *arrival* and the point of the exercise on the *first look*, which is why the two paths now read differently rather than sharing one rule.
